newsitem.title: UK: UK govt favours Natwest to take house loans.
newsitem.headline: UK govt favours Natwest to take house loans.

text.p: The British government has chosen NatWest Markets as its preferred bidder to take over the loan portfolios of the Housing Corporation and its Welsh counterpart, Housing for Wales, environment minister David Curry said on Monday.

He said in a parliamentary written answer that negotiations on the sale of loan portfolios of the two organisations, whose total face value is some 965 million stg, should be completed in the next few weeks, with the sale being completed around Easter.
"I expect a successful transfer of these loans into the private sector, and a positive ongoing relationship between housing associations and their new lender," Curry said.
The government announced in October it was to sell the portfolios provided it received satisfactory bids.

Environment Secretary John Gummer said then that for technical reasons, the sale of the portfolio of Scottish Homes would take longer than those of the Housing Corporation and Housing for Wales. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
